topic: silent analysis of the existing failure captures: the two arms show structurally different events
board_runs: none - analysis only, no audible test, no re-run
method: block-wise (2048-frame) microphone envelope, block-wise 300-360 Hz share, rail-sample census with consecutive-run lengths, microphone/reference correlation, residual rail count, all read from the stored npz

reading.zero_arm: the envelope sits at -25 dBFS for four blocks and then steps to -0.8 dBFS and stays there for three blocks (about 0.13 s). A 25 dB step within one block is not something a talker does; sustained full scale for three blocks is the signature of a runaway loop. This arm had the more severe event and completed anyway because no counter watches it.
reading.candidate_arm: the envelope never leaves the -40..-12 dBFS range; the full-scale excursion is 24 consecutive frames (0.5 ms) out of 16384, 0.2% of samples. This is a transient, not a sustained runaway.
reading.why_they_are_not_comparable: the zero arm shows a sustained step; the candidate arm shows a single short excursion. Reporting 'zero completed, candidate failed' would invert the actual severity.
reading.respecting_the_captains_caution: input full scale by itself is NOT taken as proof of regeneration in either arm. For the candidate arm it is explicitly read as a transient. For the zero arm the sustained 25 dB step is the evidence, not the rail count alone.

limits_of_this_analysis: each capture is the final 16384 frames only; for the zero arm that is the tail of a completed run, for the candidate arm it is the window ending at the guard trip
there is no microphone full-scale counter in the status file, so the rail census comes from the capture rather than from hardware
the two arms are different speech takes; the talker is not identical between them
conclusion: the live-speech comparison remains invalid as an arm comparison, but for a new reason than previously stated: the zero arm ran into a sustained runaway that no counter caught, while the candidate was stopped on a 0.5 ms transient. The candidate is not shown to be worse.
